talk.title: Is it enough?

talk.title: My class poll
talk.task: Report on people you know: “Most of my friends…”, “Very few of them…”, “None of them…”.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me yes/no questions about my friends or classmates as a group, one at a time: Have your friends ever ridden a camel? Do they read the news in English? Do they have cars? Do they like living in your city? I answer with expressions of quantity + of (Most of my friends ..., A few of them ..., Hardly any of them ..., None of them ...). Check that I use of + the/my/them correctly and never say 'most of friends'.

talk.title: Not everyone!
talk.task: Make these statements more exact: “People are friendly.” → “Most people are friendly.”
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Give me one overgeneralization at a time: Babies are born bald. / People are friendly. / People like to live alone. / Children like to read scary stories. / The rivers in the world are polluted. / The citizens of the United States speak English. I make it more accurate with an expression of quantity (Most ..., Some ..., Almost all of the ..., Hardly any ...). Check my use of of.

talk.title: Review a website
talk.task: Pick a website you know. Tell Claude what is good or bad about it, with details.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. Ask me to choose a website I know and evaluate it in 4-5 sentences, using patterns like: '___ is an example of an effective/weak website. The opening page is ... It has ... There is/are/isn't/aren't ...'. Ask me to give specific details (not 'it is interesting' but 'it has a colorful logo'). Check plural -s, noncount nouns like information (no -s), and expressions of quantity (many photos, not much information, a few bright colors).
